title: A Compass for the Current
premise: Jonah Hartwell, a salvage diver who measures life in miles rather than years, is hired to recover equipment from a wreck the navy refuses to discuss. When the radio goes silent from an expedition upriver, she discovers the missing team was searching for her father's lost survey cache — and that the navy wants it buried forever. Crossing the range ahead of the snows with two survivors of the expedition, Jonah must choose between selling out the find for a clean escape or claiming an inheritance that could kill them all. She reaches the pass as the first storm breaks, trades the cache's location to the navy in exchange for her found family's freedom, and finally stops running — measuring life in people instead of miles.
about_author: Felix Almeida is a former river guide who spent a decade leading expeditions through remote mountain watersheds before turning to fiction full-time. His novels draw on firsthand knowledge of salvage work, backcountry survival, and the quiet mathematics of grief.

chapters.title: Twelve Miles Deep
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Working a sunken navy transport off a fogbound coast, Jonah recovers a sealed case stamped with her father's initials — twelve years after his disappearance. The navy liaison aboard watches her too closely. Emotional beat: unease; the past surfacing like a body from deep water.

chapters.title: The Wreck They Won't Name
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Under cover of night she photographs documents from the case: coordinates upriver, her father's handwriting, dated three days before he vanished. The liaison, Reyes, warns her off with practiced courtesy. Emotional beat: defiance kindling; grief sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Silence on Channel Nine
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. A distress relay reports the Meridian Survey Expedition has gone dark upriver — the same coordinates. A charter pilot offers Jonah a ride to the last fuel stop if she can read the terrain maps only her father taught her to read. Emotional beat: compulsion; she boards knowing it's a trap shaped like an answer.

chapters.title: The Last Fuel Stop
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. At a decaying river town she meets Teo Vasquez, the expedition's cook, half-frozen and alone, who says the team split after finding 'something that wasn't on any map.' Navy helicopters circle overhead. Emotional beat: wary alliance; two strangers bound by absence.

chapters.title: What Wasn't on Any Map
chapters.summary: POV: Teo. Flashback chapter: the expedition found a cave system behind a waterfall containing her father's survey cache — and evidence the navy sank its own ship to hide what he discovered. Teo fled when the team leader sided with a navy man embedded in the crew. Emotional beat: dread; the scale of the lie revealed.

chapters.title: Upstream Against It
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Jonah and Teo hire a battered jetboat and run the gorge rapids while a navy patrol boat shadows them. She reads the water the way her father taught her, threading channels no chart shows. Emotional beat: exhilaration braided with fear; inheritance becoming skill, becoming identity.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sank the Ship
chapters.summary: POV: Antagonist — Commander Hale. Hale, the officer who ordered the sinking twelve years ago, receives orders to recover the cache at any cost and erase loose ends, including Jonah. We see his rationalization: one family's truth against national security. Emotional beat: cold menace; the hunter given a face.

chapters.title: Cold Camp
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Storm-bound in an abandoned trapper cabin, Jonah and Teo trade stories of the people they've lost. She admits she measures life in miles because miles can't die. He tells her about the expedition members still unaccounted for. Emotional beat: tenderness; found family taking root in frozen ground.

chapters.title: The Waterfall Cave
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. They reach the falls and enter the cave, finding the cache intact — her father's journals, mineral surveys, and proof the navy knowingly poisoned the watershed and sank the ship carrying his evidence. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fury; the inheritance is not treasure but testimony.

chapters.title: Two Survivors
chapters.summary: POV: Teo. They find expedition leader Mara Chen alive but injured in a side chamber, betrayed by the embedded navy man and left behind. Mara carries the third copy of the survey data. Emotional beat: relief shadowed by urgency; the party grows just as the window closes.

chapters.title: The Embedded Man
chapters.summary: POV: Antagonist — Sergeant Ives. Ives, the expedition's betrayer, radios Hale that the survivors have the cache and are moving for the high pass. Hale orders him to intercept before the snows seal the range. Emotional beat: tightening noose; the reader sees the trap closing from both sides.

chapters.title: The Range Ahead
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. The trio begins the ascent, racing a weather front visible as a bruise on the horizon. Mara, feverish, gives Jonah her father's final journal page: a message meant for her all along. Emotional beat: resolve hardening; the climb becomes pilgrimage.

chapters.title: Ives on the Scree
chapters.summary: POV: Teo. Ives ambushes them above the treeline. In a desperate scuffle on loose rock, Teo takes a bullet graze protecting the journals, and Ives falls to his death when the slope gives way beneath him. Emotional beat: shock and guilt; survival exacting its first real price.

chapters.title: Miles Can't Die
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Sheltering in a crevasse camp, Jonah confronts her creed: every mile she's put between herself and grief has cost her everyone she might have loved. She nearly abandons the journals to save weight and speed. Teo talks her back. Emotional beat: crisis of faith in herself; choosing people over distance.

chapters.title: Hale Closes In
chapters.summary: POV: Antagonist — Commander Hale. Hale's helicopter is grounded by the storm front; he leads a ground team up the same pass, burning supplies to move fast. His orders now explicitly include Jonah's death. Emotional beat: relentless pressure; the antagonist becomes desperate too.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. The storm hits early. Blind navigation by compass and dead reckoning — her father's craft — gets them through a whiteout that kills two of Hale's men. Mara's wound turns septic. Emotional beat: terror and competence fused; the inheritance saving their lives even as it dooms them.

chapters.title: The Pass
chapters.summary: POV: Teo. They reach the summit pass at dawn to find Hale waiting, having pushed through the night. Outnumbered and outgunned, with Mara dying, Jonah negotiates: the cache and her silence for safe passage and medical evacuation. Emotional beat: bitter surrender; the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: What the Navy Buys
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Hale honors the deal — but Jonah has already done what her father did: copied everything, and mailed one set from the last fuel stop to a journalist. She realizes Hale knows and let them go anyway, because killing them proves the story. Emotional beat: pyrrhic victory; leverage discovered in the act of losing.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Carrying Mara down through clearing skies, the three move as a unit — no longer strangers, a family forged by altitude and loss. Teo confesses he mailed nothing; Jonah did it alone, trusting no one, and understands for the first time what that habit costs. Emotional beat: humility; trust as the harder climb.

chapters.title: The Story Breaks
chapters.summary: POV: Multiple brief POVs. The journalist publishes; hearings begin; Hale is relieved of command and chooses resignation over testimony. The watershed cleanup is ordered. Jonah watches from a diner television, waiting to feel vindicated and feeling something quieter instead. Emotional beat: anticlimax as truth; justice arriving without fireworks.

chapters.title: Headstones and High Water
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Jonah visits her father's memorial stone with the original journal, leaving it open to his last page — the message to her: 'Come home by whatever current carries you.' She scatters nothing, keeps everything. Emotional beat: grief completed; the mile-measurer learning to stay.

chapters.title: A Compass for the Current
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Spring: Jonah, Teo, and recovering Mara launch a small legitimate salvage and guide outfit on the river, teaching reading-water to kids from the valley. Her compass sits on the dash, pointing not north but downriver, toward home. Emotional beat: arrival; inheritance transformed into gift, survival into living.
